lines.speaker: THIRD WITCH
lines.text: We’ll answer.

lines.speaker: FIRST WITCH
lines.text: Say, if thou’dst rather hear it from our mouths,

lines.speaker: FIRST WITCH
lines.text: Or from our masters?

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Call ’em, let me see ’em.

lines.speaker: FIRST WITCH
lines.text: Pour in sow’s blood, that hath eaten

lines.speaker: FIRST WITCH
lines.text: Her nine farrow; grease that’s sweaten

lines.speaker: FIRST WITCH
lines.text: From the murderer’s gibbet throw

lines.speaker: FIRST WITCH
lines.text: Into the flame.

lines.speaker: ALL
lines.text: Come, high or low;

lines.speaker: ALL
lines.text: Thyself and office deftly show!
[_Thunder. An Apparition of an armed Head rises._]

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Tell me, thou unknown power,—

lines.speaker: FIRST WITCH
lines.text: He knows thy thought:

lines.speaker: FIRST WITCH
lines.text: Hear his speech, but say thou naught.

lines.speaker: APPARITION
lines.text: Macbeth! Macbeth! Macbeth! Beware Macduff;

lines.speaker: APPARITION
lines.text: Beware the Thane of Fife.—Dismiss me.—Enough.
[_Descends._]

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Whate’er thou art, for thy good caution, thanks;

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Thou hast harp’d my fear aright.—But one word more.

lines.speaker: FIRST WITCH
lines.text: He will not be commanded. Here’s another,

lines.speaker: FIRST WITCH
lines.text: More potent than the first.
[_Thunder. An Apparition of a bloody Child rises._]

lines.speaker: APPARITION
lines.text: Macbeth! Macbeth! Macbeth!

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Had I three ears, I’d hear thee.

lines.speaker: APPARITION
lines.text: Be bloody, bold, and resolute. Laugh to scorn

lines.speaker: APPARITION
lines.text: The power of man, for none of woman born

lines.speaker: APPARITION
lines.text: Shall harm Macbeth.
[_Descends._]

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Then live, Macduff: what need I fear of thee?

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: But yet I’ll make assurance double sure,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: And take a bond of fate. Thou shalt not live;

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: That I may tell pale-hearted fear it lies,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: And sleep in spite of thunder.
[_Thunder. An Apparition of a Child crowned, with a tree in his hand, rises._]

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: What is this,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: That rises like the issue of a king,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: And wears upon his baby brow the round

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: And top of sovereignty?

lines.speaker: ALL
lines.text: Listen, but speak not to’t.

lines.speaker: APPARITION
lines.text: Be lion-mettled, proud, and take no care

lines.speaker: APPARITION
lines.text: Who chafes, who frets, or where conspirers are:

lines.speaker: APPARITION
lines.text: Macbeth shall never vanquish’d be, until

lines.speaker: APPARITION
lines.text: Great Birnam wood to high Dunsinane hill

lines.speaker: APPARITION
lines.text: Shall come against him.
[_Descends._]

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: That will never be:

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Who can impress the forest; bid the tree

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Unfix his earth-bound root? Sweet bodements, good!

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Rebellious head, rise never till the wood

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Of Birnam rise, and our high-plac’d Macbeth

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Shall live the lease of nature, pay his breath

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: To time and mortal custom.—Yet my heart

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Throbs to know one thing: tell me, if your art

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Can tell so much, shall Banquo’s issue ever

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Reign in this kingdom?

lines.speaker: ALL
lines.text: Seek to know no more.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: I will be satisfied: deny me this,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: And an eternal curse fall on you! Let me know.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Why sinks that cauldron? and what noise is this?
[_Hautboys._]

lines.speaker: FIRST WITCH
lines.text: Show!

lines.speaker: SECOND WITCH
lines.text: Show!

lines.speaker: THIRD WITCH
lines.text: Show!

lines.speaker: ALL
lines.text: Show his eyes, and grieve his heart;

lines.speaker: ALL
lines.text: Come like shadows, so depart!
[_A show of eight kings appear, and pass over in order, the last with a glass in his hand; Banquo following._]

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Thou are too like the spirit of Banquo. Down!

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Thy crown does sear mine eyeballs:—and thy hair,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Thou other gold-bound brow, is like the first.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: A third is like the former.—Filthy hags!

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Why do you show me this?—A fourth!—Start, eyes!

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: What, will the line stretch out to th’ crack of doom?

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Another yet!—A seventh!—I’ll see no more:—

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: And yet the eighth appears, who bears a glass

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Which shows me many more; and some I see

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: That twofold balls and treble sceptres carry.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Horrible sight!—Now I see ’tis true;

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: For the blood-bolter’d Banquo smiles upon me,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: And points at them for his.—What! is this so?

lines.speaker: FIRST WITCH
lines.text: Ay, sir, all this is so:—but why

lines.speaker: FIRST WITCH
lines.text: Stands Macbeth thus amazedly?—

lines.speaker: FIRST WITCH
lines.text: Come, sisters, cheer we up his sprites,

lines.speaker: FIRST WITCH
lines.text: And show the best of our delights.

lines.speaker: FIRST WITCH
lines.text: I’ll charm the air to give a sound,

lines.speaker: FIRST WITCH
lines.text: While you perform your antic round;

lines.speaker: FIRST WITCH
lines.text: That this great king may kindly say,

lines.speaker: FIRST WITCH
lines.text: Our duties did his welcome pay.
[_Music. The Witches dance, and vanish._]

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Where are they? Gone?—Let this pernicious hour

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Stand aye accursed in the calendar!—

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Come in, without there!
Enter Lennox.

lines.speaker: LENNOX
lines.text: What’s your Grace’s will?

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Saw you the Weird Sisters?

lines.speaker: LENNOX
lines.text: No, my lord.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Came they not by you?

lines.speaker: LENNOX
lines.text: No, indeed, my lord.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Infected be the air whereon they ride;

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: And damn’d all those that trust them!—I did hear

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: The galloping of horse: who was’t came by?

lines.speaker: LENNOX
lines.text: ’Tis two or three, my lord, that bring you word

lines.speaker: LENNOX
lines.text: Macduff is fled to England.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Fled to England!

lines.speaker: LENNOX
lines.text: Ay, my good lord.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Time, thou anticipat’st my dread exploits:

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: The flighty purpose never is o’ertook

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Unless the deed go with it. From this moment

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: The very firstlings of my heart shall be

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: The firstlings of my hand. And even now,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: To crown my thoughts with acts, be it thought and done:

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: The castle of Macduff I will surprise;

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Seize upon Fife; give to th’ edge o’ th’ sword

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: His wife, his babes, and all unfortunate souls

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: That trace him in his line. No boasting like a fool;

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: This deed I’ll do before this purpose cool:

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: But no more sights!—Where are these gentlemen?

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Come, bring me where they are.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Fife. A Room in Macduff’s Castle.

lines.text: Enter Lady Macduff her Son and Ross.

lines.speaker: LADY MACDUFF
lines.text: What had he done, to make him fly the land?

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: You must have patience, madam.

lines.speaker: LADY MACDUFF
lines.text: He had none:

lines.speaker: LADY MACDUFF
lines.text: His flight was madness: when our actions do not,

lines.speaker: LADY MACDUFF
lines.text: Our fears do make us traitors.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: You know not

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Whether it was his wisdom or his fear.

lines.speaker: LADY MACDUFF
lines.text: Wisdom! to leave his wife, to leave his babes,

lines.speaker: LADY MACDUFF
lines.text: His mansion, and his titles, in a place

lines.speaker: LADY MACDUFF
lines.text: From whence himself does fly? He loves us not:

lines.speaker: LADY MACDUFF
lines.text: He wants the natural touch; for the poor wren,

lines.speaker: LADY MACDUFF
lines.text: The most diminutive of birds, will fight,

lines.speaker: LADY MACDUFF
lines.text: Her young ones in her nest, against the owl.

lines.speaker: LADY MACDUFF
lines.text: All is the fear, and nothing is the love;

lines.speaker: LADY MACDUFF
lines.text: As little is the wisdom, where the flight

lines.speaker: LADY MACDUFF
lines.text: So runs against all reason.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: My dearest coz,

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: I pray you, school yourself: but, for your husband,

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: He is noble, wise, judicious, and best knows

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: The fits o’ th’ season. I dare not speak much further:

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: But cruel are the times, when we are traitors,

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: And do not know ourselves; when we hold rumour

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: From what we fear, yet know not what we fear,

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: But float upon a wild and violent sea

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Each way and move—I take my leave of you:

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Shall not be long but I’ll be here again.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Things at the worst will cease, or else climb upward

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: To what they were before.—My pretty cousin,

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Blessing upon you!

lines.speaker: LADY MACDUFF
lines.text: Father’d he is, and yet he’s fatherless.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: I am so much a fool, should I stay longer,

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: It would be my disgrace and your discomfort:

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: I take my leave at once.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: LADY MACDUFF
lines.text: Sirrah, your father’s dead.

lines.speaker: LADY MACDUFF
lines.text: And what will you do now? How will you live?

lines.speaker: SON
lines.text: As birds do, mother.

lines.speaker: LADY MACDUFF
lines.text: What, with worms and flies?

lines.speaker: SON
lines.text: With what I get, I mean; and so do they.

lines.speaker: LADY MACDUFF
lines.text: Poor bird! thou’dst never fear the net nor lime,

lines.speaker: LADY MACDUFF
lines.text: The pit-fall nor the gin.

lines.speaker: SON
lines.text: Why should I, mother? Poor birds they are not set for.

lines.speaker: SON
lines.text: My father is not dead, for all your saying.

lines.speaker: LADY MACDUFF
lines.text: Yes, he is dead: how wilt thou do for a father?

lines.speaker: SON
lines.text: Nay, how will you do for a husband?

lines.speaker: LADY MACDUFF
lines.text: Why, I can buy me twenty at any market.

lines.speaker: SON
lines.text: Then you’ll buy ’em to sell again.

lines.speaker: LADY MACDUFF
lines.text: Thou speak’st with all thy wit;

lines.speaker: LADY MACDUFF
lines.text: And yet, i’ faith, with wit enough for thee.

lines.speaker: SON
lines.text: Was my father a traitor, mother?

lines.speaker: LADY MACDUFF
lines.text: Ay, that he was.

lines.speaker: SON
lines.text: What is a traitor?

lines.speaker: LADY MACDUFF
lines.text: Why, one that swears and lies.

lines.speaker: SON
lines.text: And be all traitors that do so?

lines.speaker: LADY MACDUFF
lines.text: Every one that does so is a traitor, and must be hanged.

lines.speaker: SON
lines.text: And must they all be hanged that swear and lie?

lines.speaker: LADY MACDUFF
lines.text: Every one.

lines.speaker: SON
lines.text: Who must hang them?

lines.speaker: LADY MACDUFF
lines.text: Why, the honest men.

lines.speaker: SON
lines.text: Then the liars and swearers are fools: for there are liars and swearers

lines.speaker: SON
lines.text: enow to beat the honest men and hang up them.

lines.speaker: LADY MACDUFF
lines.text: Now, God help thee, poor monkey! But how wilt thou do for a father?

lines.speaker: SON
lines.text: If he were dead, you’ld weep for him: if you would not, it were a good

lines.speaker: SON
lines.text: sign that I should quickly have a new father.

lines.speaker: LADY MACDUFF
lines.text: Poor prattler, how thou talk’st!
Enter a Messenger.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Bless you, fair dame! I am not to you known,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Though in your state of honour I am perfect.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: I doubt some danger does approach you nearly:

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: If you will take a homely man’s advice,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Be not found here; hence, with your little ones.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: To fright you thus, methinks, I am too savage;

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: To do worse to you were fell cruelty,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Which is too nigh your person. Heaven preserve you!

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: I dare abide no longer.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: LADY MACDUFF
lines.text: Whither should I fly?

lines.speaker: LADY MACDUFF
lines.text: I have done no harm. But I remember now

lines.speaker: LADY MACDUFF
lines.text: I am in this earthly world, where to do harm

lines.speaker: LADY MACDUFF
lines.text: Is often laudable; to do good sometime

lines.speaker: LADY MACDUFF
lines.text: Accounted dangerous folly:  why then, alas,

lines.speaker: LADY MACDUFF
lines.text: Do I put up that womanly defence,

lines.speaker: LADY MACDUFF
lines.text: To say I have done no harm? What are these faces?
Enter Murderers.

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: Where is your husband?

lines.speaker: LADY MACDUFF
lines.text: I hope, in no place so unsanctified

lines.speaker: LADY MACDUFF
lines.text: Where such as thou mayst find him.

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: He’s a traitor.

lines.speaker: SON
lines.text: Thou liest, thou shag-ear’d villain!

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: What, you egg!
[_Stabbing him._]

lines.speaker: FIRST MURDERER
lines.text: Young fry of treachery!

lines.speaker: SON
lines.text: He has kill’d me, mother:

lines.speaker: SON
lines.text: Run away, I pray you!
[_Dies. Exit Lady Macduff, crying “Murder!” and pursued by the Murderers._]

scenes.setting: England. Before the King’s Palace.

lines.text: Enter Malcolm and Macduff.

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Let us seek out some desolate shade and there

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Weep our sad bosoms empty.

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Let us rather

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Hold fast the mortal sword, and, like good men,

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Bestride our down-fall’n birthdom. Each new morn

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: New widows howl, new orphans cry; new sorrows

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Strike heaven on the face, that it resounds

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: As if it felt with Scotland, and yell’d out

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Like syllable of dolour.

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: What I believe, I’ll wail;

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: What know, believe; and what I can redress,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: As I shall find the time to friend, I will.

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: What you have spoke, it may be so, perchance.

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: This tyrant, whose sole name blisters our tongues,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Was once thought honest: you have loved him well;

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: He hath not touch’d you yet. I am young; but something

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: You may deserve of him through me; and wisdom

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: To offer up a weak, poor, innocent lamb

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: To appease an angry god.

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: I am not treacherous.

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: But Macbeth is.

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: A good and virtuous nature may recoil

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: In an imperial charge. But I shall crave your pardon.

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: That which you are, my thoughts cannot transpose.

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Angels are bright still, though the brightest fell:

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Though all things foul would wear the brows of grace,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Yet grace must still look so.

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: I have lost my hopes.

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Perchance even there where I did find my doubts.

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Why in that rawness left you wife and child,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Those precious motives, those strong knots of love,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Without leave-taking?—I pray you,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Let not my jealousies be your dishonours,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: But mine own safeties. You may be rightly just,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Whatever I shall think.

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Bleed, bleed, poor country!

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Great tyranny, lay thou thy basis sure,

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: For goodness dare not check thee! wear thou thy wrongs;

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: The title is affeer’d.—Fare thee well, lord:

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: I would not be the villain that thou think’st

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: For the whole space that’s in the tyrant’s grasp

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: And the rich East to boot.

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Be not offended:

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: I speak not as in absolute fear of you.

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: I think our country sinks beneath the yoke;

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: It weeps, it bleeds; and each new day a gash

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Is added to her wounds. I think, withal,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: There would be hands uplifted in my right;

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: And here, from gracious England, have I offer

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Of goodly thousands: but, for all this,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: When I shall tread upon the tyrant’s head,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Or wear it on my sword, yet my poor country

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Shall have more vices than it had before,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: More suffer, and more sundry ways than ever,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: By him that shall succeed.

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: What should he be?

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: It is myself I mean; in whom I know

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: All the particulars of vice so grafted

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: That, when they shall be open’d, black Macbeth

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Will seem as pure as snow; and the poor state

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Esteem him as a lamb, being compar’d

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: With my confineless harms.

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Not in the legions

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Of horrid hell can come a devil more damn’d

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: In evils to top Macbeth.

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: I grant him bloody,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Luxurious, avaricious, false, deceitful,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Sudden, malicious, smacking of every sin

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: That has a name: but there’s no bottom, none,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: In my voluptuousness: your wives, your daughters,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Your matrons, and your maids, could not fill up

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: The cistern of my lust; and my desire

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: All continent impediments would o’erbear,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: That did oppose my will: better Macbeth

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Than such an one to reign.

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Boundless intemperance

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: In nature is a tyranny; it hath been

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Th’ untimely emptying of the happy throne,

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: And fall of many kings. But fear not yet

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: To take upon you what is yours: you may

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Convey your pleasures in a spacious plenty,

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: And yet seem cold—the time you may so hoodwink.

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: We have willing dames enough; there cannot be

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: That vulture in you, to devour so many

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: As will to greatness dedicate themselves,

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Finding it so inclin’d.

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: With this there grows

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: In my most ill-compos’d affection such

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: A staunchless avarice, that, were I king,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: I should cut off the nobles for their lands;

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Desire his jewels, and this other’s house:

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: And my more-having would be as a sauce

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: To make me hunger more; that I should forge

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Quarrels unjust against the good and loyal,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Destroying them for wealth.

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: This avarice

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Sticks deeper; grows with more pernicious root

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Than summer-seeming lust; and it hath been

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: The sword of our slain kings: yet do not fear;

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Scotland hath foisons to fill up your will,

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Of your mere own. All these are portable,

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: With other graces weigh’d.

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: But I have none: the king-becoming graces,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: As justice, verity, temp’rance, stableness,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Bounty, perseverance, mercy, lowliness,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Devotion, patience, courage, fortitude,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: I have no relish of them; but abound

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: In the division of each several crime,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Acting it many ways. Nay, had I power, I should

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Pour the sweet milk of concord into hell,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Uproar the universal peace, confound

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: All unity on earth.

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: O Scotland, Scotland!

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: If such a one be fit to govern, speak:

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: I am as I have spoken.

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Fit to govern?

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: No, not to live.—O nation miserable,

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: With an untitled tyrant bloody-scepter’d,

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: When shalt thou see thy wholesome days again,

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Since that the truest issue of thy throne

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: By his own interdiction stands accus’d,

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: And does blaspheme his breed? Thy royal father

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Was a most sainted king. The queen that bore thee,

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Oft’ner upon her knees than on her feet,

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Died every day she lived. Fare thee well!

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: These evils thou repeat’st upon thyself

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Have banish’d me from Scotland.—O my breast,

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Thy hope ends here!

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Macduff, this noble passion,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Child of integrity, hath from my soul

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Wiped the black scruples, reconcil’d my thoughts

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: To thy good truth and honour. Devilish Macbeth

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: By many of these trains hath sought to win me

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Into his power, and modest wisdom plucks me

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: From over-credulous haste: but God above

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Deal between thee and me! for even now

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: I put myself to thy direction, and

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Unspeak mine own detraction; here abjure

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: The taints and blames I laid upon myself,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: For strangers to my nature. I am yet

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Unknown to woman; never was forsworn;

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Scarcely have coveted what was mine own;

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: At no time broke my faith; would not betray

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: The devil to his fellow; and delight

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: No less in truth than life: my first false speaking

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Was this upon myself. What I am truly,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Is thine and my poor country’s to command:

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Whither, indeed, before thy here-approach,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Old Siward, with ten thousand warlike men,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Already at a point, was setting forth.

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Now we’ll together, and the chance of goodness

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Be like our warranted quarrel. Why are you silent?

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Such welcome and unwelcome things at once

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: ’Tis hard to reconcile.
Enter a Doctor.

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Well; more anon.—Comes the King forth, I pray you?

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: Ay, sir. There are a crew of wretched souls

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: That stay his cure: their malady convinces

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: The great assay of art; but at his touch,

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: Such sanctity hath heaven given his hand,

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: They presently amend.

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: I thank you, doctor.
[_Exit Doctor._]

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: What’s the disease he means?

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: ’Tis call’d the evil:

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: A most miraculous work in this good king;

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Which often, since my here-remain in England,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: I have seen him do. How he solicits heaven,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Himself best knows, but strangely-visited people,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: All swoln and ulcerous, pitiful to the eye,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: The mere despair of surgery, he cures;

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Hanging a golden stamp about their necks,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Put on with holy prayers: and ’tis spoken,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: To the succeeding royalty he leaves

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: The healing benediction. With this strange virtue,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: He hath a heavenly gift of prophecy;

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: And sundry blessings hang about his throne,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: That speak him full of grace.
Enter Ross.

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: See, who comes here?

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: My countryman; but yet I know him not.

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: My ever-gentle cousin, welcome hither.

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: I know him now. Good God, betimes remove

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: The means that makes us strangers!

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Sir, amen.

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Stands Scotland where it did?

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Alas, poor country,

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Almost afraid to know itself! It cannot

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Be call’d our mother, but our grave, where nothing,

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: But who knows nothing, is once seen to smile;

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Where sighs, and groans, and shrieks, that rent the air,

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Are made, not mark’d; where violent sorrow seems

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: A modern ecstasy. The dead man’s knell

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Is there scarce ask’d for who; and good men’s lives

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Expire before the flowers in their caps,

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Dying or ere they sicken.

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: O, relation

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Too nice, and yet too true!

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: What’s the newest grief?

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: That of an hour’s age doth hiss the speaker;

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Each minute teems a new one.

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: How does my wife?

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Why, well.

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: And all my children?

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Well too.

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: The tyrant has not batter’d at their peace?

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: No; they were well at peace when I did leave ’em.

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Be not a niggard of your speech: how goes’t?

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: When I came hither to transport the tidings,

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Which I have heavily borne, there ran a rumour

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Of many worthy fellows that were out;

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Which was to my belief witness’d the rather,

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: For that I saw the tyrant’s power afoot.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Now is the time of help. Your eye in Scotland

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Would create soldiers, make our women fight,

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: To doff their dire distresses.

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Be’t their comfort

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: We are coming thither. Gracious England hath

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Lent us good Siward and ten thousand men;

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: An older and a better soldier none

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: That Christendom gives out.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Would I could answer

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: This comfort with the like! But I have words

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: That would be howl’d out in the desert air,

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Where hearing should not latch them.

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: What concern they?

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: The general cause? or is it a fee-grief

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Due to some single breast?

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: No mind that’s honest

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: But in it shares some woe, though the main part

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Pertains to you alone.

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: If it be mine,

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Keep it not from me, quickly let me have it.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Let not your ears despise my tongue for ever,

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Which shall possess them with the heaviest sound

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: That ever yet they heard.

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Humh! I guess at it.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Your castle is surpris’d; your wife and babes

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Savagely slaughter’d. To relate the manner

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Were, on the quarry of these murder’d deer,

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: To add the death of you.

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Merciful heaven!—

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: What, man! ne’er pull your hat upon your brows.

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Give sorrow words. The grief that does not speak

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Whispers the o’er-fraught heart, and bids it break.

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: My children too?

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Wife, children, servants, all

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: That could be found.

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: And I must be from thence!

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: My wife kill’d too?

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: I have said.

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Be comforted:

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Let’s make us med’cines of our great revenge,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: To cure this deadly grief.

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: He has no children.—All my pretty ones?

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Did you say all?—O hell-kite!—All?

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: What, all my pretty chickens and their dam

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: At one fell swoop?

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Dispute it like a man.

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: I shall do so;

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: But I must also feel it as a man:

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: I cannot but remember such things were,

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: That were most precious to me.—Did heaven look on,

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: And would not take their part? Sinful Macduff,

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: They were all struck for thee! Naught that I am,

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Not for their own demerits, but for mine,

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Fell slaughter on their souls: heaven rest them now!

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Be this the whetstone of your sword. Let grief

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Convert to anger; blunt not the heart, enrage it.

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: O, I could play the woman with mine eyes,

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: And braggart with my tongue!—But, gentle heavens,

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Cut short all intermission; front to front,

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Bring thou this fiend of Scotland and myself;

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Within my sword’s length set him; if he ’scape,

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Heaven forgive him too!

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: This tune goes manly.

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Come, go we to the King. Our power is ready;

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Our lack is nothing but our leave. Macbeth

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Is ripe for shaking, and the powers above

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Put on their instruments. Receive what cheer you may;

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: The night is long that never finds the day.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Dunsinane. A Room in the Castle.

lines.text: Enter a Doctor of Physic and a Waiting-Gentlewoman.

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: I have two nights watched with you, but can perceive no truth in your

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: report. When was it she last walked?

lines.speaker: GENTLEWOMAN
lines.text: Since his Majesty went into the field, I have seen her rise from her

lines.speaker: GENTLEWOMAN
lines.text: bed, throw her nightgown upon her, unlock her closet, take forth paper,

lines.speaker: GENTLEWOMAN
lines.text: fold it, write upon’t, read it, afterwards seal it, and again return to

lines.speaker: GENTLEWOMAN
lines.text: bed; yet all this while in a most fast sleep.

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: A great perturbation in nature, to receive at once the benefit of

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: sleep, and do the effects of watching. In this slumbery agitation,

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: besides her walking and other actual performances, what, at any time,

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: have you heard her say?

lines.speaker: GENTLEWOMAN
lines.text: That, sir, which I will not report after her.

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: You may to me; and ’tis most meet you should.

lines.speaker: GENTLEWOMAN
lines.text: Neither to you nor anyone; having no witness to confirm my speech.
Enter Lady Macbeth with a taper.

lines.speaker: GENTLEWOMAN
lines.text: Lo you, here she comes! This is her very guise; and, upon my life, fast

lines.speaker: GENTLEWOMAN
lines.text: asleep. Observe her; stand close.

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: How came she by that light?

lines.speaker: GENTLEWOMAN
lines.text: Why, it stood by her: she has light by her continually; ’tis her

lines.speaker: GENTLEWOMAN
lines.text: command.

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: You see, her eyes are open.

lines.speaker: GENTLEWOMAN
lines.text: Ay, but their sense are shut.

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: What is it she does now? Look how she rubs her hands.

lines.speaker: GENTLEWOMAN
lines.text: It is an accustomed action with her, to seem thus washing her hands. I

lines.speaker: GENTLEWOMAN
lines.text: have known her continue in this a quarter of an hour.

lines.speaker: LADY MACBETH
lines.text: Yet here’s a spot.

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: Hark, she speaks. I will set down what comes from her, to satisfy my

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: remembrance the more strongly.

lines.speaker: LADY MACBETH
lines.text: Out, damned spot! out, I say! One; two. Why, then ’tis time to do’t.

lines.speaker: LADY MACBETH
lines.text: Hell is murky! Fie, my lord, fie! a soldier, and afeard? What need we

lines.speaker: LADY MACBETH
lines.text: fear who knows it, when none can call our power to account? Yet who

lines.speaker: LADY MACBETH
lines.text: would have thought the old man to have had so much blood in him?

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: Do you mark that?

lines.speaker: LADY MACBETH
lines.text: The Thane of Fife had a wife. Where is she now?—What, will these hands

lines.speaker: LADY MACBETH
lines.text: ne’er be clean? No more o’ that, my lord, no more o’ that: you mar all

lines.speaker: LADY MACBETH
lines.text: with this starting.

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: Go to, go to. You have known what you should not.

lines.speaker: GENTLEWOMAN
lines.text: She has spoke what she should not, I am sure of that: heaven knows what

lines.speaker: GENTLEWOMAN
lines.text: she has known.

lines.speaker: LADY MACBETH
lines.text: Here’s the smell of the blood still: all the perfumes of Arabia will

lines.speaker: LADY MACBETH
lines.text: not sweeten this little hand. Oh, oh, oh!

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: What a sigh is there! The heart is sorely charged.

lines.speaker: GENTLEWOMAN
lines.text: I would not have such a heart in my bosom for the dignity of the whole

lines.speaker: GENTLEWOMAN
lines.text: body.

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: Well, well, well.

lines.speaker: GENTLEWOMAN
lines.text: Pray God it be, sir.

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: This disease is beyond my practice: yet I have known those which have

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: walked in their sleep, who have died holily in their beds.

lines.speaker: LADY MACBETH
lines.text: Wash your hands, put on your nightgown; look not so pale. I tell you

lines.speaker: LADY MACBETH
lines.text: yet again, Banquo’s buried; he cannot come out on’s grave.

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: Even so?

lines.speaker: LADY MACBETH
lines.text: To bed, to bed. There’s knocking at the gate. Come, come, come, come,

lines.speaker: LADY MACBETH
lines.text: give me your hand. What’s done cannot be undone. To bed, to bed, to

lines.speaker: LADY MACBETH
lines.text: bed.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: Will she go now to bed?

lines.speaker: GENTLEWOMAN
lines.text: Directly.

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: Foul whisp’rings are abroad. Unnatural deeds

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: Do breed unnatural troubles: infected minds

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: To their deaf pillows will discharge their secrets.

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: More needs she the divine than the physician.—

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: God, God, forgive us all! Look after her;

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: Remove from her the means of all annoyance,

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: And still keep eyes upon her. So, good night:

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: My mind she has mated, and amaz’d my sight.

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: I think, but dare not speak.

lines.speaker: GENTLEWOMAN
lines.text: Good night, good doctor.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: The Country near Dunsinane.

lines.text: Enter, with drum and colours Menteith, Caithness, Angus, Lennox and Soldiers.

lines.speaker: MENTEITH
lines.text: The English power is near, led on by Malcolm,

lines.speaker: MENTEITH
lines.text: His uncle Siward, and the good Macduff.

lines.speaker: MENTEITH
lines.text: Revenges burn in them; for their dear causes

lines.speaker: MENTEITH
lines.text: Would to the bleeding and the grim alarm

lines.speaker: MENTEITH
lines.text: Excite the mortified man.

lines.speaker: ANGUS
lines.text: Near Birnam wood

lines.speaker: ANGUS
lines.text: Shall we well meet them. That way are they coming.

lines.speaker: CAITHNESS
lines.text: Who knows if Donalbain be with his brother?

lines.speaker: LENNOX
lines.text: For certain, sir, he is not. I have a file

lines.speaker: LENNOX
lines.text: Of all the gentry: there is Siward’s son

lines.speaker: LENNOX
lines.text: And many unrough youths, that even now

lines.speaker: LENNOX
lines.text: Protest their first of manhood.

lines.speaker: MENTEITH
lines.text: What does the tyrant?

lines.speaker: CAITHNESS
lines.text: Great Dunsinane he strongly fortifies.

lines.speaker: CAITHNESS
lines.text: Some say he’s mad; others, that lesser hate him,

lines.speaker: CAITHNESS
lines.text: Do call it valiant fury: but, for certain,

lines.speaker: CAITHNESS
lines.text: He cannot buckle his distemper’d cause

lines.speaker: CAITHNESS
lines.text: Within the belt of rule.

lines.speaker: ANGUS
lines.text: Now does he feel

lines.speaker: ANGUS
lines.text: His secret murders sticking on his hands;

lines.speaker: ANGUS
lines.text: Now minutely revolts upbraid his faith-breach;

lines.speaker: ANGUS
lines.text: Those he commands move only in command,

lines.speaker: ANGUS
lines.text: Nothing in love: now does he feel his title

lines.speaker: ANGUS
lines.text: Hang loose about him, like a giant’s robe

lines.speaker: ANGUS
lines.text: Upon a dwarfish thief.

lines.speaker: MENTEITH
lines.text: Who, then, shall blame

lines.speaker: MENTEITH
lines.text: His pester’d senses to recoil and start,

lines.speaker: MENTEITH
lines.text: When all that is within him does condemn

lines.speaker: MENTEITH
lines.text: Itself for being there?

lines.speaker: CAITHNESS
lines.text: Well, march we on,

lines.speaker: CAITHNESS
lines.text: To give obedience where ’tis truly ow’d:

lines.speaker: CAITHNESS
lines.text: Meet we the med’cine of the sickly weal;

lines.speaker: CAITHNESS
lines.text: And with him pour we, in our country’s purge,

lines.speaker: CAITHNESS
lines.text: Each drop of us.

lines.speaker: LENNOX
lines.text: Or so much as it needs

lines.speaker: LENNOX
lines.text: To dew the sovereign flower, and drown the weeds.

lines.speaker: LENNOX
lines.text: Make we our march towards Birnam.
[_Exeunt, marching._]

scenes.setting: Dunsinane. A Room in the Castle.

lines.text: Enter Macbeth, Doctor and Attendants.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Bring me no more reports; let them fly all:

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Till Birnam wood remove to Dunsinane

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: I cannot taint with fear. What’s the boy Malcolm?

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Was he not born of woman? The spirits that know

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: All mortal consequences have pronounc’d me thus:

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: “Fear not, Macbeth; no man that’s born of woman

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Shall e’er have power upon thee.”—Then fly, false thanes,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: And mingle with the English epicures:

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: The mind I sway by, and the heart I bear,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Shall never sag with doubt nor shake with fear.
Enter a Servant.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: The devil damn thee black, thou cream-fac’d loon!

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Where gott’st thou that goose look?

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: There is ten thousand—

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Geese, villain?

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: Soldiers, sir.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Go prick thy face and over-red thy fear,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Thou lily-liver’d boy. What soldiers, patch?

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Death of thy soul! those linen cheeks of thine

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Are counsellors to fear. What soldiers, whey-face?

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: The English force, so please you.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Take thy face hence.
[_Exit Servant._]

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Seyton!—I am sick at heart,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: When I behold—Seyton, I say!—This push

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Will cheer me ever or disseat me now.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: I have liv’d long enough: my way of life

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Is fall’n into the sere, the yellow leaf;

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: And that which should accompany old age,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: As honour, love, obedience, troops of friends,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: I must not look to have; but, in their stead,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Curses, not loud but deep, mouth-honour, breath,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Which the poor heart would fain deny, and dare not.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Seyton!—
Enter Seyton.

lines.speaker: SEYTON
lines.text: What’s your gracious pleasure?

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: What news more?

lines.speaker: SEYTON
lines.text: All is confirm’d, my lord, which was reported.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: I’ll fight till from my bones my flesh be hack’d.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Give me my armour.

lines.speaker: SEYTON
lines.text: ’Tis not needed yet.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: I’ll put it on.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Send out more horses, skirr the country round;

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Hang those that talk of fear. Give me mine armour.—

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: How does your patient, doctor?

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: Not so sick, my lord,

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: As she is troubled with thick-coming fancies,

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: That keep her from her rest.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Cure her of that:

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Canst thou not minister to a mind diseas’d,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Pluck from the memory a rooted sorrow,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Raze out the written troubles of the brain,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: And with some sweet oblivious antidote

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Cleanse the stuff’d bosom of that perilous stuff

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Which weighs upon the heart?

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: Therein the patient

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: Must minister to himself.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Throw physic to the dogs, I’ll none of it.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Come, put mine armour on; give me my staff:

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Seyton, send out.—Doctor, the Thanes fly from me.—

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Come, sir, despatch.—If thou couldst, doctor, cast

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: The water of my land, find her disease,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: And purge it to a sound and pristine health,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: I would applaud thee to the very echo,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: That should applaud again.—Pull’t off, I say.—

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: What rhubarb, senna, or what purgative drug,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Would scour these English hence? Hear’st thou of them?

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: Ay, my good lord. Your royal preparation

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: Makes us hear something.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Bring it after me.—

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: I will not be afraid of death and bane,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Till Birnam forest come to Dunsinane.
[_Exeunt all except Doctor._]

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: Were I from Dunsinane away and clear,

lines.speaker: DOCTOR
lines.text: Profit again should hardly draw me here.
[_Exit._]

scenes.setting: Country near Dunsinane: a Wood in view.

lines.text: Enter, with drum and colours Malcolm, old Siward and his Son, Macduff, Menteith, Caithness, Angus, Lennox, Ross and Soldiers, marching.

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Cousins, I hope the days are near at hand

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: That chambers will be safe.

lines.speaker: MENTEITH
lines.text: We doubt it nothing.

lines.speaker: SIWARD
lines.text: What wood is this before us?

lines.speaker: MENTEITH
lines.text: The wood of Birnam.

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Let every soldier hew him down a bough,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: And bear’t before him. Thereby shall we shadow

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: The numbers of our host, and make discovery

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Err in report of us.

lines.speaker: SOLDIERS
lines.text: It shall be done.

lines.speaker: SIWARD
lines.text: We learn no other but the confident tyrant

lines.speaker: SIWARD
lines.text: Keeps still in Dunsinane, and will endure

lines.speaker: SIWARD
lines.text: Our setting down before’t.

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: ’Tis his main hope;

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: For where there is advantage to be given,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Both more and less have given him the revolt,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: And none serve with him but constrained things,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Whose hearts are absent too.

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Let our just censures

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Attend the true event, and put we on

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Industrious soldiership.

lines.speaker: SIWARD
lines.text: The time approaches,

lines.speaker: SIWARD
lines.text: That will with due decision make us know

lines.speaker: SIWARD
lines.text: What we shall say we have, and what we owe.

lines.speaker: SIWARD
lines.text: Thoughts speculative their unsure hopes relate,

lines.speaker: SIWARD
lines.text: But certain issue strokes must arbitrate;

lines.speaker: SIWARD
lines.text: Towards which advance the war.
[_Exeunt, marching._]

scenes.setting: Dunsinane. Within the castle.

lines.text: Enter with drum and colours, Macbeth, Seyton and Soldiers.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Hang out our banners on the outward walls;

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: The cry is still, “They come!” Our castle’s strength

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Will laugh a siege to scorn: here let them lie

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Till famine and the ague eat them up.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Were they not forc’d with those that should be ours,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: We might have met them dareful, beard to beard,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: And beat them backward home.
[_A cry of women within._]

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: What is that noise?

lines.speaker: SEYTON
lines.text: It is the cry of women, my good lord.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: I have almost forgot the taste of fears.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: The time has been, my senses would have cool’d

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: To hear a night-shriek; and my fell of hair

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Would at a dismal treatise rouse and stir

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: As life were in’t. I have supp’d full with horrors;

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Direness, familiar to my slaughterous thoughts,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Cannot once start me.
Enter Seyton.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Wherefore was that cry?

lines.speaker: SEYTON
lines.text: The Queen, my lord, is dead.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: She should have died hereafter.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: There would have been a time for such a word.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Tomorrow, and tomorrow, and tomorrow,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Creeps in this petty pace from day to day,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: To the last syllable of recorded time;

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: And all our yesterdays have lighted fools

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: The way to dusty death. Out, out, brief candle!

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Life’s but a walking shadow; a poor player,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: That struts and frets his hour upon the stage,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: And then is heard no more: it is a tale

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Told by an idiot, full of sound and fury,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Signifying nothing.
Enter a Messenger.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Thou com’st to use thy tongue; thy story quickly.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Gracious my lord,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: I should report that which I say I saw,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: But know not how to do’t.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Well, say, sir.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: As I did stand my watch upon the hill,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: I look’d toward Birnam, and anon, methought,

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: The wood began to move.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Liar, and slave!

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Let me endure your wrath, if’t be not so.

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: Within this three mile may you see it coming;

lines.speaker: MESSENGER
lines.text: I say, a moving grove.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: If thou speak’st false,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Upon the next tree shalt thou hang alive,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Till famine cling thee: if thy speech be sooth,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: I care not if thou dost for me as much.—

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: I pull in resolution; and begin

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: To doubt th’ equivocation of the fiend,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: That lies like truth. “Fear not, till Birnam wood

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Do come to Dunsinane;” and now a wood

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Comes toward Dunsinane.—Arm, arm, and out!—

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: If this which he avouches does appear,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: There is nor flying hence nor tarrying here.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: I ’gin to be aweary of the sun,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: And wish th’ estate o’ th’ world were now undone.—

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Ring the alarum bell!—Blow, wind! come, wrack!

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: At least we’ll die with harness on our back.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: The same. A Plain before the Castle.

lines.text: Enter, with drum and colours, Malcolm, old Siward, Macduff and their Army, with boughs.

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Now near enough. Your leafy screens throw down,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: And show like those you are.—You, worthy uncle,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Shall with my cousin, your right noble son,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Lead our first battle: worthy Macduff and we

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Shall take upon’s what else remains to do,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: According to our order.

lines.speaker: SIWARD
lines.text: Fare you well.—

lines.speaker: SIWARD
lines.text: Do we but find the tyrant’s power tonight,

lines.speaker: SIWARD
lines.text: Let us be beaten, if we cannot fight.

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Make all our trumpets speak; give them all breath,

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Those clamorous harbingers of blood and death.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: The same. Another part of the Plain.

lines.text: Alarums. Enter Macbeth.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: They have tied me to a stake. I cannot fly,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: But, bear-like I must fight the course.—What’s he

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: That was not born of woman? Such a one

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Am I to fear, or none.
Enter young Siward.

lines.speaker: YOUNG SIWARD
lines.text: What is thy name?

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Thou’lt be afraid to hear it.

lines.speaker: YOUNG SIWARD
lines.text: No; though thou call’st thyself a hotter name

lines.speaker: YOUNG SIWARD
lines.text: Than any is in hell.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: My name’s Macbeth.

lines.speaker: YOUNG SIWARD
lines.text: The devil himself could not pronounce a title

lines.speaker: YOUNG SIWARD
lines.text: More hateful to mine ear.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: No, nor more fearful.

lines.speaker: YOUNG SIWARD
lines.text: Thou liest, abhorred tyrant. With my sword

lines.speaker: YOUNG SIWARD
lines.text: I’ll prove the lie thou speak’st.
[_They fight, and young Siward is slain._]

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Thou wast born of woman.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: But swords I smile at, weapons laugh to scorn,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Brandish’d by man that’s of a woman born.
[_Exit._]
Alarums. Enter Macduff.

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: That way the noise is.—Tyrant, show thy face!

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: If thou be’st slain and with no stroke of mine,

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: My wife and children’s ghosts will haunt me still.

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: I cannot strike at wretched kerns, whose arms

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Are hired to bear their staves. Either thou, Macbeth,

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Or else my sword, with an unbatter’d edge,

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: I sheathe again undeeded. There thou shouldst be;

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: By this great clatter, one of greatest note

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Seems bruited. Let me find him, Fortune!

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: And more I beg not.
[_Exit. Alarums._]
Enter Malcolm and old Siward.

lines.speaker: SIWARD
lines.text: This way, my lord;—the castle’s gently render’d:

lines.speaker: SIWARD
lines.text: The tyrant’s people on both sides do fight;

lines.speaker: SIWARD
lines.text: The noble thanes do bravely in the war,

lines.speaker: SIWARD
lines.text: The day almost itself professes yours,

lines.speaker: SIWARD
lines.text: And little is to do.

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: We have met with foes

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: That strike beside us.

lines.speaker: SIWARD
lines.text: Enter, sir, the castle.
[_Exeunt. Alarums._]

scenes.setting: The same. Another part of the field.

lines.text: Enter Macbeth.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Why should I play the Roman fool, and die

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: On mine own sword? whiles I see lives, the gashes

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Do better upon them.
Enter Macduff.

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Turn, hell-hound, turn!

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Of all men else I have avoided thee:

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: But get thee back; my soul is too much charg’d

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: With blood of thine already.

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: I have no words;

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: My voice is in my sword: thou bloodier villain

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Than terms can give thee out!
[_They fight._]

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Thou losest labour:

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: As easy mayst thou the intrenchant air

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: With thy keen sword impress, as make me bleed:

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Let fall thy blade on vulnerable crests;

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: I bear a charmed life, which must not yield

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: To one of woman born.

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Despair thy charm;

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: And let the angel whom thou still hast serv’d

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Tell thee, Macduff was from his mother’s womb

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Untimely ripp’d.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Accursed be that tongue that tells me so,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: For it hath cow’d my better part of man!

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: And be these juggling fiends no more believ’d,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: That palter with us in a double sense;

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: That keep the word of promise to our ear,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: And break it to our hope!—I’ll not fight with thee.

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Then yield thee, coward,

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: And live to be the show and gaze o’ th’ time.

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: We’ll have thee, as our rarer monsters are,

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Painted upon a pole, and underwrit,

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: “Here may you see the tyrant.”

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: I will not yield,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: To kiss the ground before young Malcolm’s feet,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: And to be baited with the rabble’s curse.

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Though Birnam wood be come to Dunsinane,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: And thou oppos’d, being of no woman born,

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: Yet I will try the last. Before my body

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: I throw my warlike shield: lay on, Macduff;

lines.speaker: MACBETH
lines.text: And damn’d be him that first cries, “Hold, enough!”
[_Exeunt fighting. Alarums._]
Retreat. Flourish. Enter, with drum and colours, Malcolm, old Siward, Ross, Thanes and Soldiers.

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: I would the friends we miss were safe arriv’d.

lines.speaker: SIWARD
lines.text: Some must go off; and yet, by these I see,

lines.speaker: SIWARD
lines.text: So great a day as this is cheaply bought.

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Macduff is missing, and your noble son.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Your son, my lord, has paid a soldier’s debt:

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: He only liv’d but till he was a man;

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: The which no sooner had his prowess confirm’d

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: In the unshrinking station where he fought,

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: But like a man he died.

lines.speaker: SIWARD
lines.text: Then he is dead?

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Ay, and brought off the field. Your cause of sorrow

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Must not be measur’d by his worth, for then

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: It hath no end.

lines.speaker: SIWARD
lines.text: Had he his hurts before?

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Ay, on the front.

lines.speaker: SIWARD
lines.text: Why then, God’s soldier be he!

lines.speaker: SIWARD
lines.text: Had I as many sons as I have hairs,

lines.speaker: SIWARD
lines.text: I would not wish them to a fairer death:

lines.speaker: SIWARD
lines.text: And so his knell is knoll’d.

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: He’s worth more sorrow,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: And that I’ll spend for him.

lines.speaker: SIWARD
lines.text: He’s worth no more.

lines.speaker: SIWARD
lines.text: They say he parted well and paid his score:

lines.speaker: SIWARD
lines.text: And so, God be with him!—Here comes newer comfort.
Enter Macduff with Macbeth’s head.

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Hail, King, for so thou art. Behold, where stands

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Th’ usurper’s cursed head: the time is free.

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: I see thee compass’d with thy kingdom’s pearl,

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: That speak my salutation in their minds;

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Whose voices I desire aloud with mine,—

lines.speaker: MACDUFF
lines.text: Hail, King of Scotland!

lines.speaker: ALL
lines.text: Hail, King of Scotland!
[_Flourish._]

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: We shall not spend a large expense of time

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Before we reckon with your several loves,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: And make us even with you. My thanes and kinsmen,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Henceforth be earls, the first that ever Scotland

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: In such an honour nam’d. What’s more to do,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Which would be planted newly with the time,—

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: As calling home our exil’d friends abroad,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: That fled the snares of watchful tyranny;

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Producing forth the cruel ministers

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Of this dead butcher, and his fiend-like queen,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Who, as ’tis thought, by self and violent hands

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Took off her life;—this, and what needful else

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: That calls upon us, by the grace of Grace,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: We will perform in measure, time, and place.

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: So thanks to all at once, and to each one,

lines.speaker: MALCOLM
lines.text: Whom we invite to see us crown’d at Scone.
[_Flourish. Exeunt._]
